```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# ==============================================================================
# Function 1: Extract, Synchronize & Save Usage Data to CSV
# ==============================================================================
sync_usage_data <- function(app_name = "BiodivAF",
                            account = "biodivaf",
                            csv_file = "biodivaf_usage_daily.csv",
                            from = "150d") {
  
  message("Fetching recent data from shinyapps.io...")
  raw_new <- rsconnect::showUsage(
    appName = app_name,
    account = account,
    usageType = "hours",
    from = from,
    interval = "1d")
  
  if (is.null(raw_new) || nrow(raw_new) == 0) {
    warning("No new data returned from shinyapps.io.")
    if (file.exists(csv_file)) return(read.csv(csv_file))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Format new records (strictly timestamp and hours)
  new_clean <- raw_new %>%
    mutate(timestamp = as.numeric(timestamp),
           hours = as.numeric(hours)) %>%
    select(timestamp, hours)
  
  # Merge with existing CSV if it exists
  if (file.exists(csv_file)) {
    existing_data <- read.csv(csv_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
      mutate(timestamp = as.numeric(timestamp),
             hours = as.numeric(hours)) %>%
      select(timestamp, hours)
    
    if (nrow(existing_data) > 0) {
      last_ts <- max(existing_data$timestamp, na.rm = TRUE)
      
      # Drop the trailing (partial) timestamp and add from that timestamp on
      existing_complete <- existing_data %>% filter(timestamp < last_ts)
      new_to_add <- new_clean %>% filter(timestamp >= last_ts)
      
      combined_data <- bind_rows(existing_complete, new_to_add) %>%
        distinct(timestamp, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
        arrange(timestamp)
    } else {
      combined_data <- new_clean %>% distinct(timestamp, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% arrange(timestamp)
    }
  } else {
    combined_data <- new_clean %>% distinct(timestamp, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% arrange(timestamp)
  }
  
  # Save to disk
  write.csv(combined_data, csv_file, row.names = FALSE)
  message("Successfully synced! CSV now contains ", nrow(combined_data), " days of data: ", csv_file)
  return(combined_data)
}

# ==============================================================================
# Function 2: Aggregate, Filter, and Plot
# ==============================================================================
plot_app_usage <- function(csv_file = "biodivaf_usage_daily.csv",
                           resolution = c("weekly", "daily", "monthly"),
                           time_span = "180d",
                           app_name = "BiodivAF") {
  
  resolution <- match.arg(resolution)
  if (!file.exists(csv_file)) {
    stop("CSV file '", csv_file, "' not found. Run sync_usage_data() first.")
  }
  
  # Read timestamp and derive date on the fly
  df <- read.csv(csv_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(timestamp = as.numeric(timestamp),
           date = as.Date(as.POSIXct(timestamp, origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC")),
           hours = as.numeric(hours))
  
  # 1. Filter by time span
  if (time_span != "all") {
    days_back <- switch(
      sub("^[0-9]+", "", time_span),
      "d" = as.numeric(sub("d", "", time_span)),
      "m" = as.numeric(sub("m", "", time_span)) * 30.4,
      "y" = as.numeric(sub("y", "", time_span)) * 365,
      as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9]", "", time_span))
    )
    cutoff_date <- max(df$date, na.rm = TRUE) - days_back
    df <- df %>% filter(date >= cutoff_date)
  }
  if (nrow(df) == 0) stop("No records exist within the selected time span.")
  
  # 2. Aggregate by chosen resolution
  if (resolution == "daily") {
    df_agg <- df %>% rename(period = date) %>% arrange(period)
    bar_width <- 0.8
    y_label <- "Active Instance Hours / Day"
    date_breaks <- "2 weeks"
  } else if (resolution == "weekly") {
    df_agg <- df %>%
      mutate(period = as.Date(cut(date, breaks = "week"))) %>%
      group_by(period) %>%
      summarise(hours = sum(hours, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
      arrange(period)
    bar_width <- 5
    y_label <- "Active Instance Hours / Week"
    date_breaks <- "1 month"
  } else if (resolution == "monthly") {
    df_agg <- df %>%
      mutate(period = as.Date(cut(date, breaks = "month"))) %>%
      group_by(period) %>%
      summarise(hours = sum(hours, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
      arrange(period)
    bar_width <- 20
    y_label <- "Active Instance Hours / Month"
    date_breaks <- "2 months"
  }
  
  # 3. Render plot
  ggplot(df_agg, aes(x = period, y = hours)) +
    geom_col(fill = "#1D4999", width = bar_width, alpha = 0.15) +
    geom_line(color = "#1D4999", linewidth = 0.7, alpha = 0.75) +
    geom_point(color = "#1D4999", size = 2) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = date_breaks, date_labels = "%b %Y") +
    labs(title = paste0(app_name, ": Application Usage (", tools::toTitleCase(resolution), ")"),
         x = "Period", y = y_label) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
}

apps <- rsconnect::applications(account = "biodivaf")
apps[, c("name", "status", "url")]

sync_usage_data(app_name = "BiodivAF",
                account = "biodivaf",
                csv_file = "biodivaf_usage_daily.csv")

plot_app_usage(resolution = "daily", time_span = "60d")
plot_app_usage(resolution = "weekly", time_span = "180d")
plot_app_usage(resolution = "monthly", time_span = "all")
```
